mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between INDPRO contraction events and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 3% in the same month signals a stagflation risk, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL > 103 (i.e., >3%) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such joint events.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.10) between six-month PAYEMS expansion and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months during a recovery phase signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo moving average for three consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during such recovery surges.
